clue.text: Crying: "My right back selected at outside left — a first!"

indicators.note: a first tells us that L and A come at the front of the answer
selected placed at the outside means its letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: selected means chose

indicators.note: back tells us the two words before it are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An excited football fan exclaims on picking a full-back to play out on the left wing for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right back' and 'outside left' pose as football positions; 'back' turns only My and right, giving RYM before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymose describes someone tearful, given to weeping, so it is a literary synonym for crying used as an adjective.

clue.text: Launch successor to CD with earpiece

parts.note: to lob is to launch or throw high
E follows C and D in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A firm launches a new product to replace the compact disc, complete with headphones.
explanation.walkthrough: CD looks like a compact disc but is just the letters C and D.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobe is the soft lower part of the outer ear, so playfully a piece of the ear.

clue.text: Conservative deceived and a little bit put out by punch

definitions.text: a little bit put out by punch

parts.note: to be had is to be deceived or tricked

explanation.surface: A Tory, fooled, gets knocked out by a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: The punch is a hole punch, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is the small piece of paper or card knocked out when a hole is punched, as in Florida's 2000 ballots.

clue.text: Quick maybe transgressing over this, to come back to the fold?

parts.note: to return is to come back
a crease is a fold line

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone quickly breaks the rules before returning to their flock.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a quick is a fast bowler; overstepping the line marked at the side of the crease is a no-ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is a line marking the limit of the bowler's stance, which a fast bowler may step beyond illegally.

clue.text: Man Utd initialised appeal for players

indicators.note: initialised tells us to take only the initial letter of each of the two words

parts.note: SOS is a distress call, an urgent appeal for help

explanation.surface: Manchester United make a plea for new footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: Players are musicians, not footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: Musos is informal British slang for musicians, people who play instruments.

clue.text: After drink there's urge for a snack

indicators.note: after means the urge follows the drink in the answer

parts.note: Scotch is whisky
to egg is to urge, as in egg on

explanation.surface: After a whisky someone feels like a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a hard-boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs, a British picnic snack.
explanation.definitionFit: This breaded, sausage-wrapped boiled egg is a common British snack food.

clue.text: Non-striker stands clear as bowling starts

indicators.note: starts tells us to take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman at the non-striker's end keeps out of the way as the bowler begins his run.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the non-striker is the batsman not facing the ball, but here the definition means a strikebreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike, so a non-striker in the labour-dispute sense.

clue.text: All the men and women in suits

definitions.text: All the men and women in suits

parts.words: All the men and women in suits
parts.note: not office workers but the picture figures of a deck: kings, queens and jacks in each of the four suits

explanation.definitionFit: These are the kings, queens and knaves of a pack, the only cards showing people in each suit.

clue.text: Response to joke by ventriloquist?

parts.note: a deep hearty reaction to humour, and a ventriloquist speaks seemingly from the stomach

explanation.definitionFit: A deep, hearty laugh from the stomach, the kind of reaction a very funny joke draws.

clue.text: Mole making pretty hills for example?

definitions.meaning: a small dark mark on the skin, once thought attractive on a face
a scenic place in the countryside admired for its views

explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is only a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a small facial mark thought attractive and a picturesque location visited for its scenery.

clue.text: Double acclaim from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means reading right to left, so backwards

parts.note: to acclaim is to laud or praise

explanation.surface: Two cheers ring out from the eastern side of a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' reverses LAUD in an across answer, which is written west to east.
explanation.definitionFit: Dual means twofold or having two parts, a straightforward synonym for double as an adjective.

clue.text: He turns about, resolving to chase vandal

indicators.note: resolving means the letters are broken up and settled in a new order

explanation.surface: A man spins round, determined to pursue a hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the chase is a hunt, so this vandal is one who disrupts hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Such activists try to disrupt fox hunts, so their opponents regard them as vandals of the chase.

clue.text: Running from dishonest land

parts.note: cross is old slang for dishonest or crooked, as in on the cross
a land is a country or nation

explanation.surface: Someone flees from a corrupt nation.
explanation.walkthrough: CROSS meaning dishonest is old slang, the opposite of 'on the square'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-country is a form of athletics in which competitors race over open terrain, so a kind of running.

clue.text: One getting into bother's on a rock face that's off Scottish coast

parts.note: bother's reads as bother is, and something that bothers you ails you

indicators.note: getting into means the numeral is placed inside the rock face

parts.note: a crag is a steep rugged rock face
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A troubled climber clings to a sea cliff off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts I inside CRAG; 'on' is a link. The answer is an island in the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: This granite island lies in the Firth of Clyde off Scotland's west coast, known for its curling stones.

clue.text: Air's swarming with active pilots

indicators.note: swarming means the letters mill about in a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here, giving airs

explanation.surface: The sky is crowded with busy aviators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swarming' rearranges AIRS plus ACTIVE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviatrices is the plural of aviatrix, a female aviator, so these are women pilots.

clue.text: Vivien upset about treatment involving shocking swearing

indicators.note: about means the rearranged name goes round the other piece
upset means the letters of the name are knocked out of order

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a treatment that delivers electric shocks

explanation.surface: Vivien is distressed by a course of shock therapy and lets fly with a torrent of oaths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the name into INVIVE; 'shocking swearing' reads as one phrase but splits between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Invective is abusive, insulting language, so swearing in the sense of a stream of curses.

clue.text: Trendy short skirt one removed in dare, free from responsibility

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: in places the shortened skirt inside the dare

parts.note: to dare is to defy

indicators.note: removed means one letter is taken away from the skirt

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fashionable girl in a miniskirt is challenged to take it off, without consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' leaves MNI, with the skirt's first I gone; the surface's skirt and dare are a misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To indemnify someone is to secure them against legal liability or loss, so to free them from responsibility.

clue.text: A timid type, losing heart, returning crown

indicators.note: returning means the shortened word is turned round to read backwards
losing heart means the central letters of the word are dropped

parts.note: a rabbit is slang for a timid or feeble person, especially at sport

explanation.surface: A shy person loses courage and comes back wearing a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' leaves RAIT and 'returning' turns it round; a rabbit is sporting slang for a timid, poor player.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headband, a kind of small crown worn by women or a papal crown.

clue.text: Drink about litre to satisfy

indicators.note: about means the drink goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone takes about a litre of drink to quench a thirst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like a verb in the surface but is the noun SAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To slake a thirst is to satisfy or quench it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Concern for oneself brings worry, worry, worry

parts.note: to dog is to worry or pester persistently
to eat at someone is to worry them, as in what's eating you
to dog is to worry or harass

explanation.surface: Being self-absorbed leads to endless anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: The three identical words each take a different synonym; 'brings' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruthlessly competitive world where everyone looks after their own interests is described as one of self-concern.

clue.text: Boy has to fight roughly you might say for this bonus

indicators.note: you might say signals that the words are spoken, and roughly allows a loose match in sound

parts.note: a boy is a Chris, and has said casually with the h dropped runs together
to box is to fight with the fists

explanation.surface: A lad has to scrap clumsily to earn his bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: CHRIS 'AS said quickly approximates the first word, hence 'roughly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditionally a gratuity given at Christmas to tradesmen such as postmen or milkmen, a seasonal tip or bonus.

clue.text: Sound unstressed, living in Neuschwanstein

indicators.note: living in means the answer dwells inside the castle's name

explanation.surface: A relaxed sound comes from the residents of a Bavarian castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Neuschwanstein is the fairy-tale castle in Bavaria.
explanation.definitionFit: A schwa is the neutral unstressed vowel sound, like the a in about, in phonetics.

clue.text: Tolstoy heroine in old bit of Calcutta

definitions.meaning: the tragic title character of Karenina
a small coin formerly used in India, worth a sixteenth of a rupee

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; bit means a coin, as in threepenny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is that of Tolstoy's tragic heroine and also an obsolete Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: So grisly showing much of what's out of circulation?

definitions.text: showing much of what's out of circulation
definitions.meaning: covered in spilt blood, the blood that has left the veins

explanation.walkthrough: Blood out of circulation is gore, shed blood; 'So' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gory means grisly and full of bloodshed, literally covered in spilt blood from wounds.

clue.text: Finishes off cantata or operatic solo with a bow

indicators.note: finishes off tells us to take the closing letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A singer takes a bow after completing a cantata or opera aria.
explanation.walkthrough: The bow is a violinist's bow, not a performer's bend at the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: Arco is a musical direction telling string players to play with the bow rather than plucking.

clue.text: The genome one decoded in thirty-six pages

indicators.note: decoded means the letters are worked out into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Scientists decode a genome and print it in a slim booklet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decoded' rearranges THE GENOME plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A book size in which each printed sheet is folded into eighteen leaves, making thirty-six pages.

clue.text: Crave person who's entertaining with piano

parts.note: an amusing person can be called a gas, as in he's a real gas
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A performer at the keyboard longs for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces; the definition works as in gasping for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp for something, used informally, is to crave or long for it badly.

clue.text: Woman I have put in show or musical

indicators.note: put in means the show is placed inside the other phrase

parts.note: a woman who belongs to me is my lady
a fair is a show or exhibition

explanation.surface: Someone casts their girlfriend in a stage show or musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lerner and Loewe stage hit based on Shaw's Pygmalion is a famous musical.
